signals.title: NOK/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Monetary Policy
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard registers a critical bilateral divergence: NOK leads the G10 at +1.223% (n=2 pairs) while JPY lags at -0.555% (n=7 pairs), generating an extreme 1.777% spread. Fundamental policy support underpins the move, with Norges Bank maintaining a restrictive policy rate of 4.5% against a real rate of +1.82%, whereas the BoJ kept rates unchanged at 1.25% overnight, keeping real rates deeply accommodative at -2.25%. While the BoJ declared underlying inflation has reached its 2% target and lifted its FY2027 price forecast, the decision to hold the policy rate leaves a substantial 325bp nominal policy rate deficit and an accommodative real yield backdrop weighing on the yen. This divergence drives cross-currency performance as capital rotates toward higher real-yielding currencies. Trade bias: Bullish NOK/JPY, backed by the top-tier G10 strength spread and wide real policy rate gap. Catalyst: BoJ Press Conference at 06:30 UTC. Risk: Hawkish forward guidance from the BoJ Governor during the press conference that accelerates hike timing.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Macro Stance + Options Skew Divergence
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.62 following the BoJ rate decision to hold policy rates at 1.25%, with the rate differential sustaining a +275bp Fed-BoJ policy spread (Fed 4.0% vs BoJ 1.25%) and a +271bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.94% vs TONA 1.23%). The pair remains anchored within a tight range below its SMA20 of 157.91 and SMA200 of 158.48, though holding above its SMA50 at 157.44. However, the 1-month 25-delta Risk Reversals print an extreme put skew of -2.08, indicating pronounced institutional options demand for base currency downside protection despite spot stability. Furthermore, USD/JPY correlation with VIX shows a break at corr=+0.236 versus a 252-day norm of +0.298 (z=-1.65σ), illustrating an asymmetric risk profile where market participants hedge downside aggressively into 158.00+ resistance. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, pressured by extreme downside options hedging despite positive nominal carry. Catalyst: BoJ Press Conference at 06:30 UTC. Risk: A dovish press conference that drives a spot breakout above the SMA200 at 158.48, forcing put skew unwinds.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning + Technical Downtrend
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1188 with technical trend structure confirming a firm downtrend in force, marked by the falling 20-day moving average trading below the 200-day moving average and price situated below its SMA20 (1.1206), SMA50 (1.1402), and SMA200 (1.1570). CFTC positioning data shows Leveraged Funds net short -94,138 contracts (week ending Oct 20), printing at the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z=-1.72) following a 4-week net reduction of -35,333 contracts. Structural yield differentials continue to favor the greenback, with the Fed at 4.0% vs ECB at 2.65% delivering a +135bp carry advantage (SOFR vs €STR spread at +150bp). With ESI data remaining stagnant at +4.4 and German GDP and CPI on tap, the crowded short position reflects established trend alignment rather than exhaustion. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD, supported by structural rate deficit and established downtrend below all key moving averages. Catalyst: Euro Area preliminary GDP releases starting at 06:30 UTC and German GDP at 07:00 UTC. Risk: An upside surprise in Euro Area growth prints that sparks a short-covering rally back through the SMA20 at 1.1206.

signals.title: USD/NOK — Positioning vs Retail Divergence
signals.text: USD/NOK trades at 9.237, maintaining an established downtrend below its SMA20 (9.442), SMA50 (9.404), and SMA200 (9.502) after a wide-range bearish candle expanded price 2.65 ATR below the 20-day moving average. Retail sentiment via Retail sentiment data displays an extreme 100% long / 0% short reading, directly opposing the sovereign yield momentum where the Norway 2Y spread over the US 2Y expanded +13bp over 5 sessions to +8bp (+20bp over 20 sessions). With Norges Bank policy rate at 4.5% versus Fed 4.0% offering a +50bp carry buffer for NOK alongside an elevated real policy rate of +1.82%, the retail positioning reflects trapped longs attempting to catch a falling market. This retail crowding enhances capitulation risk as technical support breaks fail to generate bid follow-through. Trade bias: Bearish USD/NOK, contrarian to the 100% retail long positioning extreme. Catalyst: Norges Bank policy meeting on 5 Nov — hold bias. Risk: A sharp correction in WTI crude below $100/bbl that halts NOK outperformance.
